name: Consumerism
summary: Consumerism, as a culture-ideology, holds that meaning, status and satisfaction in life are found in buying and using consumer goods, and that a productive economy needs ever-rising consumption. It is stated in the marketing literature of the 1950s (Lebow) and described in sociology and economics texts as a set of values rather than a programme of government.
scope: The consumerist values as defined in the Tufts module and the Oxford Dictionary of Sociology (meaning and satisfaction found in consumption, ever-growing consumption), with Victor Lebow's 1955 article as its stated form. It excludes the consumer-protection movement, consumer sovereignty in Austrian economics, and anti-consumerism. It has no programme on government, law, war or society, so most statements are null.
